introduction: On this Sunday, God appoints Ezekiel as a watchman, responsible for warning others. In the Gospel, Jesus teaches how to correct a brother or sister who sins, with patience and respect, and promises that where two or three are gathered in his name, he is there among them. Paul tells us that love is the fulfillment of the law. Let us care for one another with love and truth.

prayerOfTheFaithful.invitation: Brothers and sisters, where two or three are gathered in his name, Christ is among us. Let us pray together.
intentions: For the Church: that she may correct with gentleness and forgive with generosity. Let us pray to the Lord.
For pastors, parents and teachers, who are watchmen for others: that they may speak the truth with love. Let us pray to the Lord.
For those who are estranged from family or community: that they may be reconciled. Let us pray to the Lord.
For small groups that pray together: that they may know that Christ is in their midst. Let us pray to the Lord.
For ourselves: that we may owe no one anything except to love one another. Let us pray to the Lord.
prayerOfTheFaithful.conclusion: Lord God, your Son promised to be with us whenever we gather in his name. Teach us to correct one another with love and to pray together with faith. Through Christ our Lord.

reflection.title: In the middle of them
reflection.body:
God tells Ezekiel that he is a "watchman to the house of Israel." A watchman on a city wall warns people of danger. If Ezekiel sees someone heading toward destruction and says nothing, he shares responsibility. We are responsible for one another.

In the Gospel, Jesus gives very practical guidance on how to do this when someone sins against us. Step one: "go, show him his fault between you and him alone." Not gossip, not public shaming, but a private conversation. The goal is reconciliation: "If he listens to you, you have gained back your brother." Only if that fails should others become involved, and finally the community.

This is hard. It is often easier either to say nothing and let resentment grow, or to complain to everyone except the person concerned. Jesus asks for honesty and love together.

Then Jesus makes two promises about community. First, prayer made together has great power: "if two of you will agree on earth concerning anything that they will ask, it will be done for them by my Father who is in heaven." Second: "For where two or three are gathered together in my name, there I am in the middle of them." Christ is present whenever Christians gather in his name: at Mass, in a family praying together, in a small prayer group.

Paul gives the principle behind all of this: "Owe no one anything, except to love one another." All the commandments are summed up in one: "You shall love your neighbor as yourself." And "Love doesn't harm a neighbor."

This week, if there is someone with whom you have a problem, speak to them directly, gently and privately, instead of to others. And gather with family or friends to pray together, trusting that Christ is with you.
